q: A person is arrested on a complaint of defamation following a post alleging a scam, with no grounds communicated. At which point does the chain first become unlawful?
options: At the arrest, grounds not having been communicated as required
At the registration, defamation not being a listed ground of restriction
At the post, the allegation being unverified when it was published
At the complaint, a private grievance not sustaining criminal process
expl: Defamation is a listed ground and registration may follow; the defect is the uncommunicated arrest.
why: The second option is tempting because it sounds protective of speech, but defamation IS a listed head, so the registration itself is not the defect.
trapnote: Identify the first genuinely unlawful step, not the first step you find objectionable.

q: Advice states that once a Magistrate's permission is obtained, a night arrest of a woman is lawful in all respects. What is the flaw?
options: The permission is ineffective, night arrest of a woman being barred without exception
The permission must come from a Sessions Judge, a Magistrate lacking competence
The advice is accurate, permission curing every defect in the arrest process
The permission satisfies one safeguard only; the remaining arrest requirements continue to apply
expl: Permission answers the night-arrest condition and nothing else.
why: The advice is true so far as it goes, which is what makes it dangerous. Grounds, memo, information to a relative and production all remain.
trapnote: Partial compliance is presented as complete compliance. Ask which safeguards were not addressed.

q: Under the criminal procedure statute in force from July 2024: 1-The 24-hour production rule is retained. 2-Information may be registered irrespective of jurisdiction. 3-Police custody may be sought only in the first fifteen days. Correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Production and jurisdiction-free registration are retained; police custody was restructured.
why: The third statement describes the superseded position. The new scheme permits police custody to be sought in parts within a longer outer window.
trapnote: Where a statute has been replaced, check whether the familiar rule survived or was restructured.

q: An officer holds a person for three days, citing powers under the new criminal procedure statute. Which statement is correct?
options: The detention is lawful: the new statute extended the outer limit to ninety-six hours
The detention is unlawful: the twenty-four-hour requirement was carried into the new statute
The detention is lawful: the requirement applies only to offences punishable with death
The detention is unlawful: the new statute reduced the outer limit to twelve hours
expl: The requirement was retained unchanged; it is also a constitutional guarantee independent of the statute.
why: Two options invent a change to a figure that did not change, exploiting the general expectation that a new code alters everything it touches.
trapnote: A new statute does not alter every rule it restates. Check which figures actually moved.

q: A claim is made that because the offence of defamation was recast in the new penal statute, false allegations damaging reputation are now beyond restriction. Which statement is correct?
options: Defamation remains both a listed ground of restriction and a penal offence
Defamation is no longer a listed ground, though it remains a civil wrong
Defamation remains a listed ground but is no longer a penal offence
Defamation was removed as a ground when the offence of sedition was recast
expl: Recasting a penal provision does not touch the constitutional list of restriction grounds.
why: The confusion exploited here is between the recasting of sedition, which did occur, and defamation, which was not removed from either scheme.
trapnote: A change in the penal code cannot alter the constitutional list of grounds. They are different instruments.

q: Consider the November 2022 ruling on economically weaker sections: 1-It concerned the equality guarantees. 2-It held the ceiling not to be part of the basic structure. 3-It relaxed the arrest safeguards for reserved-category accused. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The ruling concerned equality and the ceiling; it had nothing to do with arrest safeguards.
why: The third statement is deliberately absurd in substance but plausible in form, testing whether the candidate knows what the ruling actually decided.
trapnote: News-based questions test the holding. A statement outside the subject-matter of the case is false however it is phrased.

q: Consider the 2024 nine-judge ruling on community resources: 1-It narrowed the meaning of a Directive Principle. 2-It held every privately owned resource to be a community resource. 3-It left the remedy of habeas corpus untouched. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It narrowed the directive and held the opposite on private property; liberty remedies were not in issue.
why: The third statement is true but trivially so, which tests whether a candidate rejects true statements merely because they seem beside the point.
trapnote: A statement can be both true and irrelevant. Irrelevance is not falsity.

q: A claim is made that the night-arrest safeguard and the twenty-four-hour rule become operative only after the next census. Which statement is correct?
options: Both are operative now; the census condition attaches to the delimitation of constituencies
Both are operative now; the census condition attaches to the 2023 reservation amendment
Both await the census, the safeguards forming part of the same 2023 package
Both are operative now; the census condition attaches to the new criminal statutes
expl: The census condition belongs to the women's reservation amendment alone.
why: Two options correctly say the safeguards are operative but misattribute the census condition, so identifying the operative status is only half the question.
trapnote: Getting the first limb right is not enough where the option also asserts a reason. Check both limbs.

q: Following the 2022 reorganisation of districts in Andhra Pradesh, an officer claims that a preventive detention may run six months without Board reference. Which statement is correct?
options: The Board requirement is unaffected: reorganisation alters jurisdiction, not the safeguard
The Board requirement is relaxed to six months in districts newly created
The Board requirement is unaffected because the State has not adopted the amendment
The Board requirement applies only in districts containing a Scheduled Area
expl: An administrative reorganisation cannot alter a constitutional safeguard.
why: The third option reaches the right conclusion through a wrong reason, which is a failure mode candidates rarely check for.
trapnote: A right conclusion supported by a wrong reason is a wrong option. Read the whole of each choice.

q: In an Emergency proclaimed on armed rebellion: 1-Article 19 stands automatically suspended. 2-The remedy for Articles 20 and 21 may be suspended by order. 3-A separate order suspends the remedy for others. Correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
3 only
expl: No auto-19 suspension on rebellion ground; no 20/21 suspension ever; separate order for other remedies is valid.
why: The presence of a 'none' option changes the arithmetic of guessing entirely, and here it is the answer because each statement fails on a different limb.
trapnote: Where a 'none' option appears, test every statement independently. Two failures do not imply the third is sound.
